headline: Two Pupils Die During Cauayan School Fun Run; DepEd Opens Inquiry
seoTitle: Two Pupils Die at Cauayan School Fun Run | FMB News
seoDescription: Two pupils died and two other children were injured during a school fun run in Cauayan City, with DepEd and police investigating the cause and safety measures.
deck: Two pupils died and two other children were injured during a school fun run in Cauayan City, with DepEd and police investigating the cause and safety measures.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Two pupils died and two other children were injured during a Color and Bubble Fun Run at Cauayan South Central School in Isabela on Saturday morning, October 3, according to the Department of Education and local reports citing the Cauayan City Police Station.

DepEd said a fact-finding investigation was underway and would review the activity, safety measures, equipment and the roles of those involved. The Cauayan City Schools Division Office confirmed that the incident occurred within the school premises and said it was cooperating with law enforcement and the local government.

sections.heading: Verified facts
paragraphs: GMA News reported that DepEd confirmed two learner deaths but had not yet received the police station's response when its story was published. Brigada News separately reported, citing an initial police account, that four children were taken to hospitals, where two were declared dead and two were treated for injuries.

Local reports described a possible electrical short circuit or grounding in a wet bubble area. That remains a preliminary line of investigation, not a final determination of cause. No finding of negligence, criminal liability or responsibility has been announced.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The school and division office asked the public not to circulate the children's names, photographs or videos and to avoid speculation. FMB News is withholding identifying details because the victims are minors and those details are unnecessary to explain the public-safety issue.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The deaths raise urgent questions about risk assessment, electrical safety, emergency planning and supervision during school-organized activities. Families and schools need the investigation to establish what happened before any blame or corrective action can be responsibly assigned.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the police and DepEd fact-finding reports, a confirmed technical cause, the condition of the two injured children, and any suspension, safety order or accountability measure. Until those findings are released, reports of electrocution should be treated as preliminary.
